articles.title: Cosméticos com frutos da Amazônia: jovens do AP inovam no skincare | G1
articles.standfirst: Startup nascida na Unifap usa copaíba, murumuru e açaí para desenvolver produtos de skincare. Grupo já vende para todo o país.
articles.summary: Startup da Unifap cria cosméticos com frutos da Amazônia e tecnologia coreana, desenvolvendo produtos de skincare que já são vendidos para todo o país.
articles.body:
Com tecnologia inspirada na Coreia, jovens do AP criam linha de cosméticos com frutos da Amazônia — Foto: Lenan Santos/Rede Amazônica

A rotina de cuidados com a pele (skincare) inspirada na indústria da Coreia do Sul virou tendência mundial. No Amapá , um grupo de estudantes e recém-formados no curso de Farmácia da Universidade Federal do Amapá (Unifap) resolveu utilizar a mesma tecnologia oriental, mas com um diferencial regional: ativos extraídos de plantas e frutos da floresta amazônica.

A ideia da startup Tropicácia nasceu durante uma maratona de inovação universitária, o Amapá Startup, e ganhou força nos laboratórios da instituição.

O grupo, que começou a trajetória na empresa júnior do curso, decidiu transformar o conhecimento acadêmico em um negócio independente.

"As indústrias coreanas usam os nossos ativos para desenvolver os cosméticos delas. Então nada nos impede de utilizar a tecnologia de ponta para desenvolvermos os produtos aqui mesmo", afirmou a farmacêutica e CEO da marca, Saile Lacerda.

Farmacêutica e CEO da marca, Saile Lacerda — Foto: Lenan Santos/Rede Amazônica

A linha de produtos inclui itens como gloss labial, velas de massagem, blends de argila e a espuma de limpeza facial, carro-chefe da marca, desenvolvida com essência de açaí e propriedades calmantes para a pele.

Para garantir o fornecimento das matérias-primas, os estudantes compram óleos e manteigas vegetais diretamente de produtores e comunidades extrativistas do estado, como no arquipélago do Bailique e no município de Mazagão.

Entenda os ativos amazônicos usados nos produtos:

🌿 Copaíba : óleo extraído do tronco da árvore, conhecido pela ação anti-inflamatória e cicatrizante.

🌴 Murumuru : manteiga tirada da semente da palmeira, com alto poder de hidratação.

💧 Pracaxi : óleo típico de áreas de várzea, indicado para regeneração e proteção da pele.

🌳 Açaí e Cupuaçu : frutos regionais ricos em antioxidantes, usados para nutrição e aroma.

"É uma forma de devolver para a sociedade o que aprendemos na universidade. Priorizamos os fornecedores locais para movimentar a economia circular e valorizar a riqueza do Amapá ", ressaltou Saile.

Antes de chegar ao consumidor, cada formulação passa por testes de estabilidade, avaliação sensorial (textura e aroma) e verificação de segurança em relação às normas da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa).

Apesar do crescimento e de premiações em editais de inovação, o grupo enfrenta gargalos comuns às pequenas empresas da região: a falta de infraestrutura industrial local para produção em larga escala. Por isso, os lotes ainda são manipulados de forma artesanal e manual.

Gloss labial da marca. — Foto: Lenan Santos/Rede Amazônica

Mesmo com os desafios de mercado, as vendas já ultrapassaram as fronteiras do estado por meio de plataformas digitais e do comércio eletrônico.

"Criamos a startup recentemente e ver que já estamos construindo um caminho tão sólido é emocionante. Saber que pessoas de fora valorizam um produto feito aqui com a nossa biodiversidade traz muito orgulho", comemorou a estudante de Farmácia Yasmin Santos.

Grupo começou a trajetória na empresa júnior do curso — Foto: Lenan Santos/Rede Amazônica

articles.title: Former OpenAI science lead launches Warp Science to automate wet labs with robots | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Wearing cameras and sensor gloves, the startup’s human chemists will train robots to perform various lab tasks.
articles.body:
Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil has launched Warp Sciences, a new AI startup focused on automating lab work for drug discovery. The company, which trains robots to make and test promising compounds identified by researchers, has raised $215 million at an $865 million valuation, according to Weil, who announced the startup and funding on X.

The round was led by Lightspeed, with participation from IVP, Premji Invest, and Lux Capital.

For years, biotech companies have outsourced the most labor-intensive work of synthesizing thousands of variations of molecules to contractors in China, such as WuXi AppTec. With Warp Sciences, Weil hopes to reshore that work and insulate the entire drug development process from geopolitical supply-chain risks.

Wearing cameras and sensor gloves, the startup’s human chemists will train robots to perform various lab tasks. By automating wet-lab work, Warp Sciences aims to accelerate drug discovery using robots that can operate around the clock.

articles.title: Discord now formats Markdown previews right
articles.summary: Discord’s latest update released today has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with “a bunch of symbols,” according to the company.
articles.body: Discord’s latest update released today has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with “a bunch of symbols,” according to the company. LLMs and AI agents often rely on Markdown files for instructions and context, so these improved previews could be helpful for people sharing information about AI projects on the platform. “When you upload a Markdown (.md) file, you’ll now see the file rendered all nice and neat and pretty instead of with a bunch of symbols,” Discord says. “This includes tables, formatting, all that good stuff. Totally great for when you’re doing a casual Sunday-night sharing READMEs with your friends.” Google has also improved its Markdown support, as it recently started letting users edit Markdown files directly in Docs without having to convert the files to the Docs format. Discord says its new update also lets you organize servers and channels by right-clicking the icon on the sidebar and using a new “Move to…” feature. Discord Nitro members are also now able to upload files as large as 1GB.

articles.title: The secret to fast startup growth isn't early sales, top names in tech say | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At this year’s Disrupt, Lovable GTM lead Luke Arno, Polsia's Ben Broca, and Theory Ventures’ Tomasz Tunguz gave founders some tips on how to achieve true sales success in the first 90 days.
articles.body:
The AI era has changed how fast startups can grow. Startups can grow so fast that they hit high annual recurring revenue (ARR) numbers, only to crash and burn a few months later. At this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , Lovable go-to-market lead Luke Arno, Ben Broca of the AI platform Polsia, and Theory Ventures’ Tomasz Tunguz gave founders some tips on how to set their companies up for success in those first 90 days.

Broca, whose company Polsia uses AI agents to build and run businesses with almost no human staff (Broca says he is its only employee), said that product-market fit is one of the hardest things to find right now, especially in an era when so many products can easily be copied by competitors. In response, Arno said that durable go-to-market strategies are those that can be reliably repeated.

“The most critical thing for founders or earlier-stage companies to do is develop learning density or pattern recognition for where your customers are,” Arno said. “Don’t rush to build out a top-down go-to-market motion if you’re not there yet.”

That’s why, in those first 90 days after launching a commercial product that’s ready to sell, founders should not mistake early, fast revenue for a sign that the startup is ready to scale, Arno said.

Once a startup finds use cases that work, it will only be ready to build out a sales team and go for growth after it can attract new customers by repeating what has worked. If every sale requires new tactics, the startup hasn’t truly hit product-market fit.

“If I bring on 10 new customers in 10 different ways to solve 10 different problems, sure, I brought revenue in, but I don’t have a way to go scale a go-to-market,” Arno said. “If I bring three customers in with a similar motion to solve a similar problem, now I have high confidence that I can go scale.”

Lovable, the AI app-building startup, set a lot of those early benchmarks with how fast it grew, and now founders everywhere are feeling the pressure to do the same. Lovable is valued at more than $13 billion by its investors, says its ARR has passed $600 million, and has raised more than $700 million in funding to date.

“The expectations for overall execution speed are absolutely tremendous,” Tunguz said.

But Tunguz said growth like Lovable’s is still the exception, though founders should still move fast. The pressure they feel is real, he said, because far more money flows through the startup ecosystem at every stage than when he began investing in 2008. Today, a seed deal brought in by one of his partners could just as easily be a $5 million raise, a $50 million raise, or a $500 million raise.

The winners all focus on one thing: understanding their customers well enough to know what will keep them around even after any hype subsides.

“Community building is very important and being close to customers is very important,” Broca said. He said founders can send emails and throw events, and he personally likes to talk to a lot of his customers: “The general rule is always to be talking to customers.”

articles.title: Arc browser sunsets December 22 as The Browser Company doubles down on Dia | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Arc was fiercely beloved by a dedicated group of enthusiasts, but it never quite became the mass-market Chrome alternative its makers once envisioned.
articles.body:
The Browser Company is sunsetting its design-forward Arc browser on December 22, 2026, and directing users to Dia, its AI-first browser. The company announced the decision on Thursday, citing the rising cost of keeping a browser secure in the age of AI.

“Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI,” the company wrote.

“Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that’s where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.”

The wind-down is staged into three parts. As of Thursday, new Arc accounts can no longer be created. On November 23, Arc Search on iOS and Android will lose its AI features, including “Browse for Me.” Users will no longer be able to sign in or sync tabs, though the app will continue functioning as a basic local browser.

On December 22, Arc will stop working entirely on Mac and Windows. Accounts will be deactivated, and personal data will be deleted within 30 days. Arc Search will also be removed from the Google Play Store.

While The Browser Company claims Dia now surpasses Arc in speed, stability, and security benchmarks, user reactions on social media were largely disappointed , with many reviving requests for the company to make Arc open source.

But CEO Josh Miller previously pointed out that Arc is built on the Arc Development Kit (ADK) — a proprietary internal SDK that is also the core engine powering Dia. Open-sourcing Arc would mean giving away Dia’s intellectual property.

“While we’d love to open-source Arc someday, we can’t do that meaningfully without also open-sourcing ADK,” Miller previously noted. “And ADK is still core to our company’s value.”

For users making the switch, Dia will carry over equivalents of several core Arc features. Users can still swipe between different work and personal environments using Dia’s “Profiles” (formerly Arc’s Spaces). Arc’s signature vertical tabs will remain as an optional sidebar layout, while Folders have been rebranded as “Pinned Tab Groups.”

Passwords, bookmarks, extensions, and history will seamlessly transfer to Dia. Arc features will remain free in Dia, with AI optional.

The shutdown officially closes a chapter that began in 2025, when the startup stopped active feature development on Arc. The Browser Company — which was acquired by Atlassian for $610 million in 2025 — conceded at the time that while early adopters loved the browser’s novel interface, the “ novelty tax ” and complexity limited mainstream adoption. Arc was fiercely beloved by a dedicated group of enthusiasts, but it never quite became the mass-market Chrome alternative its makers once envisioned.

articles.title: Rivian buys world model startup to accelerate self-driving ambitions | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Third Dimension's technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian's reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator.
articles.body:
EV maker Rivian has acquired Third Dimension, a U.K. startup founded by veterans of the gaming and autonomous vehicle industries that uses AI to turn images and videos into lifelike 3D worlds.

Rivian isn’t getting into gaming, but it does want to leverage Third Dimension’s technology to turn real-world data into 3D worlds that can accelerate the development of its advanced driver-assistance features and the self-driving system for the robotaxis it plans to supply to Uber.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The 15-person team at Third Dimension, most of whom are based in the U.K., will be absorbed into Rivian’s autonomy and AI team led by James Philbin. The acquisition also gives Rivian an opportunity to expand its AI hub in London, Philbin said in an exclusive interview.

Third Dimension, which was founded by CEO Tolga Kart and Piotr Sokólski in 2024, raised $7 million in seed funding from venture capital firms, including Abstract Ventures, MVP, Soma Capital, and Solari Capital. While the company’s technology was built to speed up video game development, the founders saw other potential applications, including defense and autonomous vehicles.

Now, under Rivian, they’ll be focused on automated driving.

“The team is excited to be able to focus on one problem,” Kart told TechCrunch in the interview. “I think as a small company, having to serve many, many different masters is very hard, and so we’re very excited to come work on a problem that has such an amount of scale, where our technology makes a true difference.”

Simulation is a critical tool for autonomous vehicle developers, who use it to train and validate self-driving systems. Historically, these simulators were built on rendering or video game engines and often relied on synthetic data. These virtual environments might look like the real world, but a gap between the two remains, Kart said. The workaround typically requires feeding the simulators ever-larger amounts of data in hopes of closing that quality gap.

Third Dimension’s technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian’s reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator.

Rivian collects driving data from tens of thousands of R1S pickup trucks, R1S SUVs, delivery vans, and R2 SUVs on the road today — essentially any vehicle whose owner has enabled external camera sharing. Rivian uses that data, which is aggregated and anonymized, to build training models for driving. According to Philbin, Rivian gets more than 400,000 sequences uploaded from its customer fleets per day.

Third Dimension’s tech will allow Rivian to simulate complex driving conditions without having to wait for rare real-world edge cases to occur, Philbin said.

This story is developing and will be updated.

articles.title: IIT Indore selects 5 tech startups from 104 for incubation
articles.summary: IIT Indore’s LAUNCHPAD incubates 5 startups chosen from 104, spanning AI defence drones, precision farming robotics, AR/VR training and digital healthcare solutions.
articles.body: Times News NetworkIndore: From AI-powered surveillance drones for defence applications to robotic solutions for precision farming and remote physiotherapy, five technology startups have been selected from 104 applications for incubation at IIT Indore’s LAUNCHPAD Innovation Centre.IIT Indore director Prof Suhas S Joshi, who interacted with the founders, encouraged them to focus on indigenous technologies and solutions addressing real-world challenges. He stressed the need to strengthen domestic technological capabilities and convert research into commercially viable products.Among the selected ventures, Rages India Revolution Pvt Ltd is developing AI-powered autonomous surveillance drones equipped with swarm intelligence for defence, security and industrial monitoring. PragyanikAI Pvt Ltd is working on AI, robotics and IoT-based precision agriculture solutions capable of automating spraying, seeding, weeding and irrigation.GoUrbano Services Pvt Ltd is developing AI-powered augmented and virtual reality solutions for medical, clinical and STEM training, while Remote Physios is building IoT-enabled physiotherapy devices supported by augmented reality and AI-driven clinical assistance.The fifth startup, Few Good Humans Services Pvt Ltd, is developing a digital healthcare marketplace connecting patients and families with verified, medically qualified attendants for on-demand care.Officials said the five startups were selected through multiple rounds of screening, interactions, presentations and evaluation by an investment committee. The incubation programme will provide access to industry experts, mentors, investors, financial institutions and technology specialists to help startups validate their products, secure funding and explore commercial opportunities.LAUNCHPAD Incubation and Innovation Centre at Sinhasa IT Park is being operated by IITI DRISHTI CPS Foundation, IIT Indore, in collaboration with Madhya Pradesh State Electronics Development Corporation (MPSeDC).IITI DRISHTI CPS Foundation is also serving as the knowledge and technical evaluation partner for MP Semiconductor Summit 2026.As part of MP Semicon Startup Challenge, the top 10 shortlisted startups were scheduled to participate in an offline pitching round at LAUNCHPAD on Thursday.
